subject: Intermittent stalled LLM session reported by MarketBoard - triage closed
messages:
From: Oliver Hayes <oliver@marketboard.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent stalled generation in production (request IDs attached)

Hi Rishi,

We're seeing intermittent 'hangs' from Redwood in production starting yesterday evening. Affected sessions appear to stall mid-generation for ~30-90s and then either return partial output or time out on our side. This is impacting our customer flows.

Examples: request IDs attached in the CSV (marketboard-session-ids-20270714.csv) and I've included our client SDK logs (customer-sdk-logs-oliver-20270714.txt).

Environment: us-west-2 region, model pinned to "rw-instruct-v3-medium", SDK v1.12.0, no proxy. Latency spikes started around 2027-07-14T01:00:00Z and are sporadic.

Can your team confirm there's an issue on Redwood's side? If helpful, we can route traffic to a fallback for a bit.

Thanks,
Oliver Hayes
Head of Integrations
MarketBoard

Hi Oliver — thanks for the signal and for attaching the artifacts. I'm looping in Stephanie (CS lead) and Markus (SRE) to help triage.

Quick summary of what we'll do immediately:
- Replay the request IDs through our tracing/backfill system and check for errors, throttles, or atypical routing.
- Inspect inference runtime logs for the pinned model and the associated GPU host health metrics.
- Verify whether any autoscaling or routing events coincide with the timestamps you provided.

One question up front: are the request IDs in the CSV the Redwood request_id header you get back from the API or your own internal correlation IDs? If they're your internal IDs, please include the Redwood request_id (x-rw-request-id) when possible — that maps directly to our traces.

We'll follow up in ~2–4 hours with initial findings. If anything is urgent, please call the support line (I included Stephanie to assist in real time).

—Rishi
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the help.

Subject: Re: Intermittent stalled generation in production (request IDs attached)

Hi Oliver — quick closure note after our investigation. tl;dr: we were not able to reproduce or find platform-side evidence that would explain the observed stalls for the provided timestamps and artifacts.

What we checked:
- Traces: we backfilled the absolute times you provided and looked for matching x-rw-request-id values and matching client IPs. There are no corresponding error codes, server-side timeouts, or retries recorded in our traces for the supplied timestamps.
- Runtime & host health: model-serving hosts in us-west-2 showed normal GPU utilization and no OOM events or kernel timeouts.
- Routing & autoscaling: no large routing changes, host drains, or autoscaler flaps occurred in the window you shared.
- Networking: no upstream load-balancer errors or TCP retransmission anomalies were observed from our side.

Notes from Markus (SRE): the partial payload pattern you described is consistent with client-side timeouts or network interruptions that occur after our streaming chunks are returned. If you can capture the x-rw-request-id next time, we can map the trace immediately and avoid ambiguity.

Suggested next steps (to help isolate):
- If possible, enable capturing of the x-rw-request-id header on your SDK requests (it's returned on every response) and forward that when you see an issue.
- Toggle a short experiment directing a small percentage of traffic to the fallback and capture the full exchange for a failed session (including raw TCP/HTTP, if possible).
- Share the SDK version (you noted v1.12.0) and whether you have any local proxies or retries configured that could affect streaming.

As a courtesy for the disruption, Stephanie has authorized a one-time 10% monthly credit on the invoice while you run an extended test if you deem it helpful — I'll coordinate offline if you want to accept. That doesn't imply platform blame, just a goodwill gesture while you validate.

If you capture a clear x-rw-request-id or if the issue recurs, please reopen this thread and we'll pivot to a deeper, live session with SRE.

Thanks, and sorry for the interruption to your flows.
—Rishi
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
